messages:
Incidents Bot: :rotating_light: PAGER — Dedicated pool 'opaltech-prod' showing sustained GPU util >95% for 18m, queue depth 240, error rate up to 2.3% (baseline ~0.1%). Tenant: OpalTech (enterprise-VPC). Severity P2. thread_ts=1812349999
Sam R: Ack. I'm oncall and looking. Pulling job/queue metrics now. Can someone drop the Grafana link?
Li W: Grafana: https://grafana.redwood/ops/d/opaltech/dedicated-pool?orgId=1 — seeing many long-running sessions, KV cache misses spike, model memory at ~98% on several nodes.
Sam R: Running quick check of pods: ```kubectl get pods -l pool=opaltech-prod -o wide
NAME                               READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE
inference-0-opaltech-prod-0        4/4     Running   0          6d
inference-1-opaltech-prod-0        4/4     Running   0          6d
inference-2-opaltech-prod-0        3/4     Running   2          4h
inference-3-opaltech-prod-0        2/4     Running   5          30m
```
Sam R: Queueing is happening at the ingress layer; requests are piling on worker queue. This is a dedicated pool for OpalTech, so no other tenants are affected, but their own requests are degrading.
Emily K: FYI I pinged OpalTech (AE channel). They say they have an unexpected batch eval kicked off 20m ago and they didn't notify us. Asking them to pause now.
Nina S: Customer support thread says they tried to pause but the job is orchestrated by a partner service and may take ~30m to stop.
Sam R: Options: 1) Ask customer to pause (preferred). 2) Manual burst from shared capacity (requires capacity override). 3) Evict/kill long-running inferences (risky for customer). Suggest we request a short burst and also apply temporary rate-limits to background routes.
Li W: Note: Dedicated pools do not autoscale automatically for this customer (policy). We can allocate a manual burst: `rbctl allocate-burst --pool opaltech-prod --gpus 2 --ttl 1h` — needs approval from capacity owner.
Emily K: Customer now says they cannot fully pause; they request a short burst. They're willing to pay for extra capacity.
Sam R: Dexter / capacity team, can we get a 2-GPU temporary allocation? I'm requesting approval now. @Dexter M
Dexter M: I see available headroom in shared capacity. Approve 2 GPUs for 1h to OpalTech. I'll trigger the allocation.
Dexter M: Executing: `rbctl allocate-burst --pool opaltech-prod --gpus 2 --ttl 1h --owner dexter` — running now.
Sam R: Applying immediate mitigation: also setting tenant quota to throttle background jobs while we stabilize: `rbctl set-quota --tenant opaltech --rps 200 --routes background`
Dexter M: Allocation result: ```{"status":"success","pool":"opaltech-prod","added_gpus":2,"ttl":"1h","expires_at":"1812354067"}``` Burst added.
Incidents Bot: :white_check_mark: Burst allocation succeeded — +2 GPUs to opaltech-prod until 1812354067.
Li W: Monitoring metrics — queue depth dropping: 240 -> 120 -> 48 within ~4 minutes. Median latencies for interactive routes back to SLO. Background job tail still high but improving. Error rate down to ~0.4%.
Sam R: Good. We'll leave burst in place and monitor. Handoff: I'll hand to night SRE in 30m. Nina, can you take watch once I go off? Key items: burst TTL 1h, confirm job end or extend/terminate, monitor queue depth and error rate.
Nina S: Ack — I'll take watch at 18:45 UTC. If queue depth >50 after 30 minutes or error rate >1% escalate to eng-runtime.
Emily K: I'll coordinate with OpalTech to get a permanent mitigation plan — either scheduled windows for heavy batch jobs or opt-in autoscale for their dedicated pool. Also logging a billing follow-up for the extra GPU time.
Sam R: For post-incident: owners: eng-runtime (Li) to look at model memory / cache behavior, capacity policy (Dexter) to propose a safer self-serve burst flow for enterprise pools, account (Emily) to coordinate customer scheduling and billing.
Sam R: Quick notes on risk: manual burst is safe here (single-tenant), but we should avoid opaque bursts that shift load. Recommend a policy update: require AE sign-off + automatic guardrails (max burst %).
Li W: Added a short-term guard: limit per-tenant in-flight requests to 400 while burst active.
Incidents Bot: Current status: mitigated -> resources added + rate-limited background jobs + customer engaged. Monitoring mode.
Sam R: Closing this thread for active operations; I'll keep watch until handoff. Follow-ups: postmortem scheduled tomorrow 09:00 PT. If anything regresses ping this thread or page oncall.
Nina S: Will monitor and update if anything changes.
Emily K: Customer engaged and agreed to schedule changes; thanks team.
Sam R: Summary (to include in postmortem): root cause - large unnotified batch job by OpalTech filling dedicated pool; mitigation - manual burst + tenant rate-limits + customer coordination; impact - increased latency and errors for ~20-40m, no cross-tenant impact; action items - autoscale policy discussion, improved AE/runbook for customer batch windows, permanent quota defaults.
